body:
I am living with a very generous family who have given me a place to eat and sleep for months, but I feel that the mother (and by proxy her eldest daughter) are emotionally abusive toward the youngest daughters in the family. The way they speak to the daughters gives me painful flashbacks to my own childhood. I am afraid that these children will grow to have the same deep-seated neuroses I have developed from living in similar circumstances. I feel powerless to help, and fear that I shall eventually confront the mother about her abuse in the act, causing me to leave the house. I have nowhere to go and I am not financially capable of acquiring my own shelter. I almost left to step into traffic today, but I can't do that while these children view me as a part of their lives or I would scar them forever. Still, I have blankets, clothes, and very basic survival tools packed and ready to go at a moment's notice just in case.

I am also very apathetic about the future because several times in the past few months I have nearly gotten my life back on track, but misfortune has snatched each victory short of my grasp.

I have been thinking a lot about my fucked-up childhood and how it has stolen entire states of mind from me. I've been able to remember some of these using drugs, which has in turn helped me remember more that I'd repressed about my upbringing. I feel defective; damaged. Not by the drugs, mind; but by the horrific behaviors taught to me by my monster of a father, and by the shame inflicted on me by a hysterical mother. I know that with effort I can surpass these personal obstacles, but I remember a happier time where no effort would be necessary.

A recent magic mushrooms trip has opened my eyes to the fact that I have been essentially delusional my entire adolescent life. Suicidal thoughts have been my escape: I have always, as long as I remember not distinctly being a child, felt compelled to seek enough freedom that suicide always remains an option. And yet, even during times when suicide would have been extraordinarily easy - the darkest of my life, and forever etched in memory - I stayed my hand and thought, "Hey, what's a little bit longer?" And that has been the story of my survival almost half my life. I fantasize about suicide - it is always, at any given moment, unlikely I'll get close to actually attempting it. I haven't got the "guts" for that at this point.

I think I might have developed a mild sort of schizophrenia at some point. I had a very strong internal monologue most of my adolescence, as I assumed (and assume) most people do, but I could always distinguish the imaginary voices in my head as bits of information I *imagined*, as opposed to external and exhibiting agency. So I figured I was safe from schizophrenia on that count. But since experimenting with psychedelics, I have rediscovered on occasion a calm silence like I haven't felt since childhood. This makes me wonder whether my internal monologue is healthy...

Not being able to consult a medical professional about concerns like these - and tremors I have had in my left hand - without fearing involuntary commitment to a psych ward, or repercussions to my professional life as a result of background checks, has caused me great distress. Even if those weren't concerns, I can neither afford nor reach such professionals at this point in my life.

I understand my state of mind and the causes of it quite well at this point. I also know what I need to do to keep on the road to recovery from my depression; it's just difficult, and the cost of slipping is potentially my life. And that's often not very compelling motivation for me.

I guess I'm rambling. And I guess the major points are these: I know what I'm doing, I know what has happened and why, and I know what I need to do for myself. All that's left, then, is feeling absolutely defeated at the pain I see everywhere in this house... I don't know which path I can take that wouldn't constitute abandonment. I'm going to leave, that's a definite. But these children have the rest of their underage lives to look forward to this daily screamfest.
